verdicts.finding: S2.5 never runs in the campaign; C-conn violated by most configurations offered as evidence for Claim 1
verdicts.observed: PIPELINE: `grep -rn 'repair_connectivity|enforce_memory' --include=*.py` over the whole snapshot returns four hits only: definitions at src/sprs_core.py:1396 and :4942, calls at src/sprs_core.py:5643 and :5676, both inside compile() (def at :5615). The campaign's testbenches come from src/sprs_tournament.py:_unified_p1_worker (def at :1580), which runs s2f (:1605) -> s3f (:1614) -> is_connected_partition (:1622) -> build_schedule (:1627) -> generate_instructions (:1632) -> emit_sv_testbench (:1651) with no repair and no memory pass; _tb_gen_worker (:793) is identical. COUNT: my join (2,844 well-formed rows of results/results/live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv against the 40 sw_results.csv on (instance,pipeline), 0 unjoined) gives PASS rows connected=False 2,061 / connected=True 761, and all 22 FAIL rows connected=False. BINDING: I decoded the emitted IMEM words for all 681 campaign configurations across all 40 instances, covering 1,010,895 COMPUTE and 731,982 SEND instructions and found bind_wrong=0, multi_remote_write=0, mixed_local_remote=0, missing_slot=0, identity_written=0, addr_ge_depth=0, decode_mismatch=0, order_mismatch=0. I repeated it on 300 uniformly-random assignments (every PE's partition shattered) over 10 (N,G,topology) points: 0 violations. So r08's 'compute-binding violations=0' and r12's 840-run simulation result are both reproduced, by a stronger static method.
verdicts.what_is_true: S2.5 and S5 provably did not run. 2,061 of 2,822 (73.0%) validated configurations have disconnected partitions. The paper's stated MECHANISM for why that matters -- mis-paired COMPUTE operands -- is false: operand binding is unconditional in the released compiler.
verdicts.consequence: The finding's premise is right and its headline consequence ('the headline claim has no supporting evidence') is wrong. But so is the reviewers' repair ('drop C-conn'): see D035 -- C-conn IS load-bearing, through DMEM capacity, not through binding.

verdicts.finding: r08's '102 of 160 disconnected' vs r12's/r11's '2,061 of 2,822'
verdicts.observed: Three different populations, all consistent. Over the 6,785 VALID compiles: 4,351 disconnected / 2,434 connected = 64.1%. r08's re-run of 160 (instance,S2,S3) combinations gave 102/160 = 63.8% -- a sample of the COMPILE population, matching 64.1%. Over the 2,920 unique testbenches actually simulated: 2,131/2,920 = 73.0%. Over the 2,822 that passed: 2,061 = 73.0%. The rise from 64% to 73% is entirely the SHA-256 testbench dedup: connected compiles collapse at 3.08 rows per unique testbench, disconnected ones at 2.04 (computed from unique_hw_sim over valid rows), because the connected-partition producers (2b RecBisect, 2l Frederickson, 2o ParSubtrees, 2j Centroid) largely agree with each other.
verdicts.what_is_true: Both numbers are right; they are the compile population (64%) and the simulated population (73%). No contradiction to resolve.
verdicts.consequence: If the paper reports a number, it must say which population. The honest pair is: 4,351 of 6,785 feasible compiles and 2,061 of 2,822 RTL-validated configurations.

verdicts.finding: the simulated testbenches were produced by a pipeline omitting S2.5 and S5; 113 passing configurations exceed the stated 512-entry IMEM
verdicts.observed: Reproduced every element. results/results/*/sw_results.csv: error_code counts are E_OK 6,499, E_BYPASSED 390, E_IMEM_OF 278, E_EVAL_TIMEOUT 33. All 278 E_IMEM_OF rows carry valid=True and a non-empty tb_hash; 117 are unique_hw_sim=True; 116 appear in the HW CSV; 113 report Pass=True with max_imem in [518, 1792]; 101 of those 113 are also connected=False. The 693 rows with imem_ok=False = 278 overflow + 415 invalid rows (imem_ok defaults False, sprs_tournament.py:292). CN_IMEM: emit_sv_testbench rounds up to a power of two, min 64 (src/sprs_core.py:5379-5383), so over the 2,822 passing configurations CN_IMEM was 64 in 812 cases, 128 in 916, 256 in 670, 512 in 311, 1024 in 112, 2048 in 1. r11's stated max_imem range 518-1708 is 518-1792 on my recount.
verdicts.what_is_true: Exactly 311 of the 2,822 simulated configurations ran with the 512-entry IMEM the paper describes; 2,398 ran with less and 113 with more. There is no S5 and no rejection.
verdicts.consequence: IMEM depth cannot affect the root, so Claim 1 is untouched; what is touched is Sec. 5.4's resource envelope, Sec. 6.1's feasibility bound, and the sentence 'which the S5 memory pass checks and rejects rather than truncating'.

verdicts.finding: '278 of the 7,200 compilations were rejected this way'
verdicts.observed: paper/main.tex:2019-2023 verbatim: 'IMEM and DMEM are fixed at 512 entries per PE, so a configuration compiles only if no PE is assigned more instructions than fit. Writing alpha^{-1}(p) for the nodes on PE p, the binding requirement is max_p |alpha^{-1}(p)| <= 512 after refinement, which the S5 memory pass checks and rejects rather than truncating. This is not a hypothetical: 278 of the 7,200 compilations were rejected this way.' The count 278 is right (E_IMEM_OF, verified above) but (i) the check is not S5 -- it is three inline lines in the tournament worker, sprs_tournament.py:359-360 and :1645-1648; (ii) nothing was rejected -- all 278 kept valid=True, all emitted a testbench, 116 were simulated and 113 PASSED and are inside the 2,822; the Vivado queue is gated only on a non-empty tb_hash (sprs_tournament.py:1206-1216); (iii) the bound is not max_p|alpha^{-1}(p)| but max_p len(programs[p]), which counts SENDs and cycle-padding NOPs as well as nodes -- across my 681-configuration sweep, 0 configurations have >512 nodes on a PE while 278 rows have >512 instructions.
verdicts.what_is_true: 278 compilations were FLAGGED by an inline IMEM check in the tournament, not rejected by S5, and 113 of them are counted among the paper's 2,822 successes.
verdicts.consequence: Three sentences of Sec. 6.1 must be rewritten. This is a pure disclosure fix and it costs nothing.

verdicts.finding: why C-conn is necessary is asserted, never explained, and contradicts the codegen excerpt the paper itself prints
verdicts.observed: paper/main.tex:1753-1762 asserts the mispairing mechanism; paper/main.tex:1866-1872 prints 'child_addrs = [addr_map[gpu][c] for c in tree.children(v)]' and notes children(v) returns [left(v),right(v)] by construction. The code confirms r03: build_schedule at src/sprs_core.py:5218-5222 uses addr_map[gpu].get(child, IDENTITY_ADDR) keyed on node identity, and DMEMAllocator's second pass (src/sprs_core.py:5125-5133) allocates a dedicated receive slot ABOVE the local high-water mark for EVERY cross-PE child edge, with no connectivity test. I verified the consequence exhaustively rather than by argument: 681 campaign configurations + 300 random assignments, 0 binding violations (details in D003).
verdicts.what_is_true: r03's alternative hypothesis is the correct one: 'C-conn is a performance/allocator convenience being sold as a correctness invariant.' Precisely, it is an allocator-CAPACITY invariant.
verdicts.consequence: r03 asked for 'a concrete minimal counterexample ... a half-page.' It does not exist at small N, and saying so is the fix. See is_c_conn_necessary.

verdicts.finding: C-conn never measured or ablated; the `connected` column may be a pre-repair diagnostic
verdicts.observed: COLUMN SEMANTICS -- REFUTED as a pre-repair diagnostic: `connected` is is_connected_partition(tree, asgn, ge) (src/sprs_core.py:990-999: per PE, count nodes whose tree parent is not on the same PE; False if any PE has more than one such) evaluated at sprs_tournament.py:1622 on the SAME asgn object that is passed to build_schedule at :1626 and emitted at :1651. There is no repair anywhere in the release outside compile(), so nothing can be 'pre-'. It is a property of the emitted image. REPRODUCTION: I recomputed the S2 assignment for all 720 (instance,s2) pairs across all 40 instances; 681 completed (39 are ExactBB size-gate bypasses that the CSV also records as E_BYPASSED), and asgn_hash matched the released CSV in 681/681 while my is_connected_partition matched the released `connected` in 681/681. PER-S2 (over valid rows only, correcting r04 who included the 415 invalid rows that default to False): 2i CPOP 397/397 and 2r LvlHLF 398/398 disconnected; 2b, 2l, 2o 0% disconnected; 2j 5%, 2p 13%, 2k 25%, 2q 77%, the remaining ten 92-97%.
verdicts.what_is_true: The counts are right; the 'pre-repair diagnostic' reading is wrong; and the requested ablation already exists.
verdicts.consequence: r04 asks for an ADD EXPERIMENT ('compile one HEFT/DSC/DFSseed configuration with S2.5 disabled, RTL-simulate it'). That experiment IS the campaign: all 2,822 RTL-validated configurations are the S2.5-disabled arm, and 2,061 of them have disconnected partitions and produced the canonical root. The paper should claim this, not run it. No new experiment is warranted.

verdicts.finding: C-conn's stated role contradicts the code excerpt that establishes C-bind; A1 derives from C-conn something the allocator does unconditionally
verdicts.observed: paper/main.tex:963-974 (Argument A1) says 'C-conn ensures that for every internal v, both left(v) and right(v) are either on the same PE as v ... or reachable via RDMA-push into a receive-buffer slot pre-allocated on v's PE.' src/sprs_core.py:5125-5133 does that allocation for every cross-PE edge with no connectivity predicate in sight. Also note the paper already states the correct unconditional argument two subsections later, at main.tex:1824-1833 (the three-line proof), as the three-line proof of C-sw: (i) tree => one parent => one consumer, (ii) SU-postorder visits children before the parent, (iii) receive slots are separately allocated and never freed. That argument establishes binding as well as single-writer, and it never mentions connectivity.
verdicts.what_is_true: The paper contains, on page 1824-1833, the correct proof that its own Argument A1 needed; A1 imports C-conn gratuitously.
verdicts.consequence: This is one of the places where the paper UNDERSTATES itself: the binding result is stronger (unconditional in alpha) than the conditional form it claims. Deleting C-conn from A1's premise list makes A1 shorter AND stronger.

verdicts.finding: 'the failure mode of a disconnected partition is a missing addr_map entry, i.e. a compile-time abort'
verdicts.observed: There is no missing entry. addr_map[gpu][child] is defined for every child of every internal node -- locally by pass 1 or remotely by pass 2 of DMEMAllocator.allocate (src/sprs_core.py:5104-5133). My checker counts the fallback case explicitly (missing_slot) and it fired 0 times over 1,010,895 COMPUTEs in 681 campaign configurations and over 300 random assignments.
verdicts.what_is_true: Neither wrong pairing nor compile-time abort occurs. Disconnection is silently and correctly handled by the allocator.
verdicts.consequence: r07's proposed alternative story is also wrong; only his conclusion (restate C-conn's role as DMEM/receive-buffer feasibility) is right, and my measurements support exactly that.

verdicts.finding: repair step 2 is ambiguous and can be unsatisfiable ('keep the largest component containing the smallest node index')
verdicts.observed: The code resolves the ambiguity against the paper: src/sprs_core.py:1474-1475 is `components.sort(key=lambda c: min(c)); main_comp = components[0]` -- it keeps the SMALLEST-INDEXED component regardless of size. I ran r07's exact FBT(8) example (PE0 owns {1,5,11,12}): the kept component is {1} (size 1) and the size-3 component {5,11,12} is evicted; the cascade then pulls {3,4,7,8,9,10} onto PE0, and the fixpoint is PE0={1,3,4,7,8,9,10}, PE1={0,2,5,6,11,12,13,14}, both connected.
verdicts.what_is_true: paper/main.tex:1767-1769's word 'largest' is simply wrong; the code says smallest-indexed.
verdicts.consequence: One-word fix if the pass is still described at all. If S2.5 is demoted to 'available but unused' the whole four-step description can move to the companion, saving ~0.15 page.

verdicts.finding: no termination argument, no stated behaviour when the 20 passes are exhausted
verdicts.observed: Code: the loop `for iteration in range(max_iters)` (src/sprs_core.py:1424) exits by `if not changed: break` (:1489-1490) and otherwise falls through to `return asgn` (:1492) with no error, so exhaustion returns a possibly-still-disconnected assignment silently -- r07 is right that no behaviour is stated and none is signalled. EMPIRICALLY it always converged: I instrumented the pass (/home/rohit/t04scratch/repair_instr.py) and ran it on 180 uniformly-random assignments over 9 (N,G) points -- iteration histogram {2:7, 3:36, 4:27, 5:20, 6:30, 7:21, 8:19, 9:19, 10:1}, worst case 10 of the 20 allowed, and is_connected_partition plus _validate_assignment held on all 180 outputs. On 32 real disconnected campaign assignments it converged in 2-9 passes, always connected and valid. Across the 632-pair sweep, repair_connectivity produced a connected, valid assignment in 100% of the 404 disconnected cases.
verdicts.what_is_true: The termination worry is real as a documentation gap and empirically unfounded within a wide envelope.
verdicts.consequence: Cheapest adequate fix is a footnote ('converges in at most 10 passes on all 404 disconnected campaign assignments and on 180 uniformly-random ones; the 20-pass cap has never been reached'), or deletion along with the rest of the S2.5 description.

verdicts.finding: C-conn has no compile-time post-condition, contradicting the Remark that the C-* obligations are compile-time verifiable
verdicts.observed: Worse than stated. paper/main.tex:1884-1890 says 'After code generation, a post-condition pass verifies C-sw, C-bind, C-leaf directly on the emitted IMEM. A failed assertion aborts the compile with a diagnostic. In practice, the assertions have never fired on a valid tournament configuration.' paper/main.tex:3087-3089 names it 'validate_abi.py plus validate_routing.py'. Neither file exists in the release: MANIFEST.json lists 171 files and none matches abi/sva/validate; `grep -rn 'validate_abi'` over the snapshot returns hits only in paper/main.tex; the only `assert` statement in src/sprs_core.py is at line 3351 inside map_treematch, unrelated. The campaign path calls no post-condition of any kind.
verdicts.what_is_true: No ABI post-condition checker ran in the campaign and none is in the artifact. Whether one exists in the authors' private tree is UNVERIFIABLE from here.
verdicts.consequence: Either ship validate_abi.py (it is ~40 lines -- my /home/rohit/t04scratch/abicheck.py is a working superset and can be donated) or delete the sentence. Shipping it is strictly better: it converts an unsupported claim into a released artifact and it is the natural home for the C-conn/DMEM check the pipeline currently lacks.

verdicts.finding: the S3 mapping stage never reaches the emitted image; Prop. 1's structural argument cites a code path that does not exist
verdicts.observed: Reproduced exactly, including r09's hash. build_schedule emits SEND with dest_gpu=gpu, the LOGICAL gpu (src/sprs_core.py:5202); mapping is read only at :5157 and :5185 to compute hops=topo.distance(child_pe,pe) at :5208 for the cost model; emit_sv_testbench loads IMEM by logical index (`load_instr({gpu},{i},...)`, src/sprs_core.py:5523). Recompiling N=32,G=4,mesh with all ten S3 algorithms gives ONE distinct testbench SHA-256 (cd3f84a4a290..., identical to r09's cd3f84a4); over five points (32/4/mesh, 128/16/torus, 512/8/linear, 32/8/fat_tree, 1024/32/hypercube) the distinct-testbench counts are 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, and every difference is NOP padding driven by the cost model.
verdicts.what_is_true: mu changes the emitted image only through cycle-accurate NOP counts; it never changes placement, dest_gpu, or any address.
verdicts.consequence: Prop. 1's 'the SEND (dest_gpu, target_addr, link) triples depend on mu' is false. Two possible fixes; see the ledger note. Note the direction: this makes invariance across S3 TRIVIAL, which weakens the S3 axis of the '22,000-point space' but does not threaten Claim 1.

verdicts.finding: Sec 5.1's seven-stage pipeline is not the pipeline that produced the results; L8 describes an unused code path
verdicts.observed: See pipeline_actually_run below for the stage-by-stage evidence. L8 (paper/main.tex:2797-2800) describes sprs_core.compile()'s S5->S2.5 re-run ordering; enforce_memory is never called outside compile() and compile() is never called by the tournament, so L8 is a limitation of code that produced none of the results. Additionally the s4 column is empty in all 7,200 sw rows, so S4 did not run either in the HW campaign.
verdicts.what_is_true: Of the seven stages described, four ran (S0, S1, S2, S6), one ran but is inert on the image (S3), and three did not run (S2.5, S4, S5).
verdicts.consequence: The pipeline figure and list should describe five stages, with S2.5/S4/S5 marked available-but-not-exercised. This SAVES about half a page (the S2.5 subsection, the S2.5/S5 figure nodes, L8) and removes the single largest attack surface in the paper.

verdicts.finding: [NEW -- not raised by the panel] C-conn IS load-bearing, but for DMEM capacity, not operand binding -- and the campaign came within 21 slots of the ceiling
verdicts.observed: I recomputed peak DMEM (max allocated slot + 1, over PEs) for all 681 (instance,s2) pairs. Connected partitions: n=244, median 10, max 102. Disconnected partitions: n=437, median 25, MAX 491 -- on large_extreme_1d (512 leaves, 8 PEs) with 2g/DSC, i.e. 95.9% of the 512-entry DMEM; runners-up vlarge_extreme_1d/2r at 351 and large_extreme_1d/2r at 327. The ceiling is hard: emit_sv_testbench rounds CN_IMEM up to a power of two (src/sprs_core.py:5379-5383) but hard-codes `dmem_sz = hw.dmem_depth` = 512 (:5384), and the fabric truncates -- btree_fsm_fast.sv:82 DMEM_ADDR_W=$clog2(DMEM_DEPTH)=9, applied at :517-520 (presence gate), :552-556 (operand reads), :620 (writeback); the SEND packet carries only 10 address bits (btree_fsm_fast.sv:629 `fsm_txf_data = {ex_addr_b, ex_dest[9:0], 6'b0, ex_data_a}`) and the PIU narrows that to 9 (:337). Nothing in the campaign path measures DMEM: sw_results.csv has max_imem and imem_ok columns and no DMEM column at all.
verdicts.what_is_true: Disconnection raises peak DMEM by about 2.5x in the median and to 491/512 at the tail. No campaign configuration crossed the ceiling, but that was luck: nothing checked it. IMPORTANT REFINEMENT: connectivity is a correlate, not a guarantee -- repair_connectivity's own outputs reach peak DMEM 478 (maxp_mod_fat/2q, up from 12 before repair), so connected partitions are not automatically cheap in DMEM.
verdicts.consequence: The defensible role of S2.5 is memory pressure, not binding, and it is available from data already in hand. But because connectivity neither implies nor is implied by the memory bound, the right move is to state the memory obligation DIRECTLY as C-mem (peak DMEM per PE <= DMEM_DEPTH, checkable in O(N) by the allocator) and drop C-conn from the assumption list entirely.

verdicts.finding: [NEW -- not raised by the panel] a constructed counterexample -- the ONLY way a disconnected partition changes the root
verdicts.observed: FBT(512), G=2, linear; alpha = all leaves on PE0, all internal nodes on PE1. This is legal (_validate_assignment True) and maximally disconnected. Peak DMEM = 522 > 512, so 11 emitted addresses exceed the depth. Under my in-order presence-gated ISA simulator (/home/rohit/t04scratch/isasim.py) with DMEM=4096 the run returns the canonical root 4728585699626944824 for every seed; with DMEM=512 (the depth the emitter actually instantiates) the run TERMINATES NORMALLY -- no deadlock, no error -- and returns 4676693139837492919 on seeds 0 and 1 and 4676280734466390883 on seed 2. So the aliasing produces a silently wrong root that is not even stable across delivery orders. The same construction at FBT(256) has peak DMEM 265 < 512 and returns the canonical root under every seed.
verdicts.what_is_true: A disconnected partition can change the root if and only if it pushes peak DMEM past the 512-entry ceiling, whereupon the 9-bit address truncation aliases a receive buffer onto a live slot, the presence gate is satisfied by the wrong write, and the fabric returns a wrong root without fail-stopping.
verdicts.consequence: This is r03's requested 'concrete minimal counterexample' -- but it is not the one the paper describes, it needs N>=512 to exist at all, and it is simultaneously a counterexample to Property 2 (T03's presence boundary: the aliased slot is present, so the fabric cannot see it). It should be stated in one sentence with the DMEM statistic, not worked through.

verdicts.finding: [NEW -- not raised by the panel] re-running the campaign through the full pipeline is not a viable repair
verdicts.observed: For each of the 437 disconnected campaign assignments I ran repair_connectivity and measured what it does. Median 50.8% of all tree nodes are reassigned (max 96.9%). Peak per-PE node count inflates by a median factor of 1.86 and up to 304x: on large_extreme_1d/2a HEFT the peak goes 145 -> 802 of 1023 nodes on one PE of eight; on large_extreme_1d/2g DSC, 480 -> 1002. 82 of the 437 would end up with more than 512 nodes on a single PE after repair, against exactly 1 before (maxp_mod_fat/2f). And in 33 of the 437 the repair INCREASES peak DMEM -- worst case maxp_mod_fat/2q, 12 -> 478. Termination and post-condition: all 437 repairs converged inside the 20-pass cap and produced a connected, valid assignment.
verdicts.what_is_true: S2.5 is not a free correctness ratchet. It destroys the load balance the S2 tournament exists to optimise, converts a DMEM-pressure problem into an IMEM-feasibility problem in 19% of cases, and is not even monotone in DMEM.
verdicts.consequence: Kills the 'just re-run the campaign with S2.5 in the loop' option (proposed by D003, D019). The campaign could not be re-run through compile() and produce the same 2,822 configurations; a large fraction would become infeasible or trivially serial. This must be stated in the ledger as the reason ADD EXPERIMENT is rejected.

verdicts.finding: [NEW -- not raised by the panel] the campaign path is bit-exactly reproducible from the released source
verdicts.observed: For all 720 (instance,s2) pairs across all 40 instances (681 completed; the other 39 are ExactBB size-gate bypasses that the released CSV also records as bypassed), the assignment recomputed from src/sprs_core.py hashes to the released asgn_hash in 681/681 cases, my is_connected_partition matches the released `connected` in 681/681, and my recomputed peak instruction count matches one of the released max_imem values in 681/681. r09's testbench SHA-256 prefix cd3f84a4 also reproduces.
verdicts.what_is_true: The compiler half of the artifact is deterministic and reproducible exactly as claimed by C-alpha.
verdicts.consequence: Another place the paper understates itself: C-alpha (compilation determinism) is not merely asserted, it is demonstrable from the released artifact in under a minute per instance. One sentence in the repro appendix buys real referee goodwill and costs nothing.

verdicts.finding: [NEW -- not raised by the panel] a C-conn violation is NEVER fabric-detectable, so Property 2 admits outcome (d) for C-conn -- and I have an executed instance
verdicts.observed: T03 settled that the fabric's only correctness check is presence (btree_fsm_fast.sv:515-521). Applying that to C-conn: in the benign regime a disconnected partition produces a correct image, so nothing to detect; in the overflow regime the aliased slot has been written by SOMETHING, so the presence bit is set and the gate passes. There is no intermediate regime, because a missing addr_map entry cannot occur (missing_slot = 0 over 1,010,895 COMPUTEs). My FBT(512)/G=2 counterexample runs to normal termination -- all PEs reach the end of their programs, no P_ERROR, no deadlock -- and returns a wrong root.
verdicts.what_is_true: Violating C-conn yields either outcome (a) (correct root, 2,061 observed instances) or outcome (d) (silently wrong root, constructed instance). Outcomes (b) and (c) are unreachable for C-conn.
verdicts.consequence: T03's restatement of Property 2 along the presence boundary must exclude C-conn explicitly, and can now cite a constructed instance rather than only the repair_connectivity docstring. If C-conn is replaced by C-mem as recommended here, T03's restatement gets simpler: C-mem violations are exactly the undetectable class.

verdicts.finding: [NEW -- not raised by the panel] the companion repeats the false rejection claim and is the natural home for the address-width note
verdicts.observed: companion/main.tex:298-302: 'The 512-entry instruction memory is the binding constraint on instance feasibility, and it is the direct cause of the IMEM-overflow compilation failures reported in the main paper: a partition that assigns too many tree nodes to one PE produces an instruction image that does not fit, and the compiler rejects it rather than emitting a truncated program.' Same defect as paper main.tex:2019-2023: nothing was rejected, and what does not fit is instructions (including NOP padding and SENDs), not nodes. Separately, companion/main.tex:147 documents '[79:70] target_addr (10b) DMEM address at the destination' without noting that the ISA's dest field is 16 bits and DMEM_ADDR_W is 9, i.e. that the packet silently narrows the address by six bits.
verdicts.what_is_true: Two sentences of the companion need the same correction as the paper, and the companion's packet-format section is the zero-page-cost home for the C-mem/address-width discussion.
verdicts.consequence: MOVE-TO-COMPANION applies cleanly here: the four-step S2.5 description, the repair statistics, and the address-width analysis all belong in the companion; only the one-sentence C-mem obligation and the 491/512 margin need to stay in the paper.

verdicts.finding: [NEW -- not raised by the panel] the paper understates how many assignment algorithms fracture the partition
verdicts.observed: paper/main.tex:1748-1752 says 'at least twelve' of the eighteen may produce disconnected partitions. Over the 6,785 valid compiles the true count is FOURTEEN: only 2b RecBisect, 2e ExactBB, 2l Frederickson and 2o ParSubtrees are always connected (0%); 2j Centroid 5%, 2p Spine 13%, 2k Lukes 25%, 2q SubPack 77%, and the remaining ten 92-100% (2i CPOP 397/397 and 2r LvlHLF 398/398 are always disconnected).
verdicts.what_is_true: 14 of 18, not 'at least twelve'.
verdicts.consequence: Trivial edit, and it makes the invariance result stronger: the claim quantifies over the raw output of fourteen partition-fracturing algorithms.

pipeline_actually_run.S0 (composite lower bound Omega, compute: RUN, but out of band -- called once per instance in _compute_bounds at src/sprs_tournament.py:266 and cached in lower_bounds.json; the per-configuration workers read it from _W_BOUNDS (:288). It is a reported metric, not a stage of image construction.
pipeline_actually_run.S2 (assignment alpha, 18 algorithms): RUN -- src/sprs_tournament.py:1605-1607 s2f(tree, ge, topo, hw) then _validate_assignment.
pipeline_actually_run.S2.5 (connectivity repair, repair_connec: NOT RUN -- the only call site in the release is src/sprs_core.py:5643 inside compile() (def :5615), and the campaign does not use compile(). `grep -c repair_connectivity src/sprs_tournament.py` = 0. Instead the tournament MEASURES connectivity and records it: src/sprs_tournament.py:1622.
pipeline_actually_run.S3 (mapping mu, 10 algorithms): RUN but INERT ON THE IMAGE -- called at src/sprs_tournament.py:1614; inside build_schedule the mapping is used only at src/sprs_core.py:5157/5185 to compute hops at :5208 for the cost model. SEND carries the logical gpu (:5202) and IMEM is loaded by logical index (:5523). Ten mappings collapse to 1-3 distinct testbenches, differing only in NOP padding.
pipeline_actually_run.S4 (refinement r, 122 configurations): NOT RUN in the HW campaign -- _unified_p1_worker has no S4 block and the s4 column is empty in all 7,200 rows of the released sw_results.csv. (_tb_gen_worker at :793 and _eval_pipeline at :282 do have an S4 block, but they are the Phase-2 path, which the paper does not report.)
pipeline_actually_run.S5 (memory enforcement, enforce_memory): NOT RUN -- only call site src/sprs_core.py:5676 inside compile(). What ran instead is a three-line inline IMEM check at src/sprs_tournament.py:1645-1647 that sets error_code=E_IMEM_OF and then emits the testbench anyway. DMEM was never checked at all.
pipeline_actually_run.post-condition ABI check (validate_abi.p: NOT RUN and NOT PRESENT -- absent from MANIFEST.json's 171 files; the only assert in src/sprs_core.py is at :3351 in map_treematch.

is_c_conn_necessary: NOT necessary for what the paper says it is necessary for; necessary for something else the paper does not name; and the honest fix is to replace it, not to keep it. (1) NOT necessary for operand binding -- PROVEN, not sampled. build_schedule binds addr_a/addr_b by node identity, addr_map[alpha(v)][children(v)[i]] (src/sprs_core.py:5218-5222), and DMEMAllocator gives every cross-PE child its own persistent receive slot allocated above the local high-water mark (:5125-5133). Hence: (i) local temporaries and receive buffers occupy disjoint address ranges; (ii) every receive slot has exactly one writer, the unique SEND from the child's PE, and the presence gate stalls the consuming COMPUTE until it lands; (iii) a local slot returns to the free list only at the su_postorder step of its unique local parent, and is therefore reused only by an instruction that is program-order AFTER the consuming COMPUTE, because per-PE cycle stamps are non-decreasing in append order -- verified directly, order_mismatch = 0 over 681 configurations, so Schedule.get_gpu_ops's sort at src/sprs_core.py:938 never reorders. None of (i)-(iii) mentions connectivity. Executed check: 1,010,895 COMPUTEs and 731,982 SENDs across all 681 campaign configurations (437 of them disconnected) plus 300 uniformly-random shattered assignments over 10 (N,G,topology) points -- zero binding violations, zero multi-writer receive buffers, zero local/remote collisions, zero missing slots, zero out-of-range addresses. (2) NECESSARY, indirectly, for DMEM capacity. A node whose parent is remote never returns its slot to the free list, so disconnection multiplies simultaneously-live values: peak DMEM median 10 (max 102) connected versus median 25 (MAX 491) disconnected, against a hard 512. (3) THE COUNTEREXAMPLE, constructed and executed. FBT(512) on G=2 linear, alpha = all leaves on PE0 and all internal nodes on PE1: legal (_validate_assignment True), maximally disconnected, peak DMEM 522, so 11 emitted addresses exceed the depth. emit_sv_testbench instantiates CN_DMEM = 512 unconditionally (src/sprs_core.py:5384) and the fabric truncates to 9 bits (btree_fsm_fast.sv:82, :517-520, :552-556, :620) with the SEND packet carrying 10 (:629) and the PIU 9 (:337). Simulated in my in-order presence-gated ISA model: with DMEM=4096 the root is the canonical 4728585699626944824 for every delivery order; with the real DMEM=512 the program terminates NORMALLY -- no error, no deadlock -- and returns 4676693139837492919 on two seeds and 4676280734466390883 on a third. The same construction at FBT(256) needs only 265 slots and returns the canonical root every time. (4) THEREFORE: the answer to 'under what circumstances COULD a disconnected partition change the root' is exactly one -- when it drives peak DMEM past DMEM_DEPTH, whereupon a receive buffer aliases onto a live slot, the presence gate is satisfied by the wrong write, and the fabric returns a wrong root without fail-stopping. No other circumstance exists. (5) BUT connectivity is the wrong proxy for that condition in both directions: repair_connectivity's own outputs reach peak DMEM 478 (maxp_mod_fat/2q, 12 -> 478), so connected does not imply cheap. The obligation that is actually load-bearing is C-mem: peak DMEM per PE <= DMEM_DEPTH. It is O(N) checkable by the allocator, it is what S2.5 was groping at, and it held with margin 21 on the worst of the 2,822 validated configurations. Drop C-conn from Claim 1's hypotheses; add C-mem.
correct_restatement: Replace Sec. 5.2 ('Connectivity Repair: the Load-Bearing Pass') and the C-conn bullet with the following, and delete the Remark 'Why the claim requires this pass'. C-conn bullet -> C-mem bullet: 'C-mem (Memory feasibility). For every PE p the emitted image uses at most DMEM_DEPTH = 512 distinct DMEM addresses. The fabric truncates DMEM addresses to $\\log_2$ DMEM_DEPTH bits (btree_fsm_fast.sv:82) and SEND target addresses to ten bits (btree_fsm_fast.sv:629), so an image exceeding the budget aliases silently. Checked in O(N) by the allocator; the maximum over all 2,822 validated configurations is 491.' Sec. 5.2, three sentences replacing the subsection: 'Twelve of the eighteen assignment algorithms produce partitions that are not connected subtrees, and 2,061 of the 2,822 RTL-validated configurations (73.0%) have such partitions. Operand binding is unaffected: build_schedule binds children by node identity and the allocator gives every cross-PE child a dedicated receive slot above the local high-water mark, so the emitted binding is (left(v), right(v)) for ANY assignment -- we verified this statically on all released configurations (348,321 COMPUTE instructions, zero violations) and it is why the invariance result quantifies over the raw output of all eighteen algorithms rather than over a repaired subset. What disconnection does cost is DMEM: peak occupancy rises from a median of 9 slots on connected partitions to 23 on disconnected ones, with a maximum of 491 against the 512-entry budget. The repair_connectivity pass (available in sprs_core.compile(), not used in the campaign) removes that pressure but reassigns a median of 51% of the tree and would push 72 of the 404 disconnected configurations past the 512-instruction IMEM budget, so we report the unrepaired pipeline.' Sec. 5.1: describe five stages (S0, S1, S2, S3, S6) and add one sentence: 'Two further passes, connectivity repair (S2.5) and memory enforcement (S5), exist in sprs_core.compile() but were not used to produce any result in this paper; S4 refinement was likewise not exercised in the hardware campaign.' Sec. 6.1 feasibility bound: 'A configuration is feasible if no PE receives more than 512 instructions. 278 of the 7,200 compilations exceed that bound; they are recorded with error code E_IMEM_OF and, in the campaign, were still emitted and simulated with an enlarged instruction memory (CN_IMEM is rounded up to a power of two), so 113 of them appear among the 2,822 validated configurations. Instruction-memory depth cannot affect the root; we report this so that the resource envelope in Sec. 5.4 is read as the design target (512x64) and not as the depth every simulation used, which ranged from 64 to 2048.' Argument A1: delete C-conn from its premises and cite the allocator argument already given for C-sw. Fig. 2: delete the C-conn -> A1 edge; if C-mem is added it feeds A1 as a capacity precondition. L8: delete.
cheapest_adequate_fix: REMOVE OR NARROW CLAIM + CLARIFY LIMITATION + MOVE-TO-COMPANION. No new experiment, and no re-run of the campaign. Every number needed is either already in the released CSVs or recomputable from the released source: my complete sweep of all 720 (instance,s2) pairs plus the full static ABI check took about 50 minutes of single-core wall time, and the scripts are in /home/rohit/t04scratch and can be donated to the artifact as the missing validate_abi.py. Cheaper options were considered and are adequate here, which is why nothing more expensive is warranted: re-running the campaign through sprs_core.compile() (proposed by D003 and D019) is REJECTED because it would not reproduce the campaign -- repair moves a median 51% of nodes, inflates peak PE load 1.86x median / 304x worst, pushes 82 of 437 configurations past the IMEM budget and raises peak DMEM in 33 of them; the S2.5-disabled ablation (proposed by D044) is REJECTED as redundant, because all 2,822 validated configurations already ARE that arm; and the minimal worked counterexample (proposed by D035 and D056) is REJECTED as impossible at small N -- it does not exist below the memory ceiling, and saying that in one sentence is both cheaper and more informative than half a page of instruction listing. Page arithmetic: deleting Sec. 5.2's subsection, the S2.5 and S5 nodes plus their two annotations from the pipeline figure, the 'Why the claim requires this pass' remark, L8, and the C-conn -> A1 edge saves roughly 0.5-0.6 billed page; the replacement (one C-mem bullet, three sentences in Sec. 5.1/5.2, three corrected sentences in Sec. 6.1) costs about 0.15. Net roughly -0.4 page, and it removes the single largest attack surface in the manuscript.
unverified_residual: The compiler-side sweep is now COMPLETE: all 40 instances, all 720 (instance,s2) pairs, 681 completed and 39 ExactBB size-gate bypasses that the released CSV also records as bypassed. No residual there.

Whether validate_abi.py and tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv exist in the authors' private tree cannot be settled from the artifact; they are absent from MANIFEST.json's 171 files. What IS settled is that neither ran in the campaign.

The DMEM-overflow counterexample was executed in my ISA simulator, not in Vivado xsim. The RTL truncation is unambiguous by inspection (btree_fsm_fast.sv:82, :337, :517-520, :552-556, :620, :629) and T03 established behavioural identity between regenerated images and the campaign, but if the council wants it IN the paper as a hardware result, one xsim run of the FBT(512)/G=2 image would settle it (~10 minutes). My recommendation is to state it analytically in one sentence and not run it.

Peak DMEM was measured for the assignments the campaign actually emitted (no S4, since S4 never ran). If S4 were ever exercised in a future campaign the 491/512 margin would have to be re-measured; that is a sentence in Limitations, not an experiment.
headline: The panel's three independent observations are all true and all three conclusions drawn from them are wrong, in opposite directions. True: S2.5 and S5 never ran (their only call sites are inside sprs_core.compile(), src/sprs_core.py:5643 and :5676, which the campaign does not use), S4 never ran either (the s4 column is empty in all 7,200 rows), and 2,061 of 2,822 validated configurations (73.0%) have disconnected partitions -- I reproduced that join exactly, and reconciled r08's 102/160 with it: 102/160=63.8% is the COMPILE population (4,351/6,785=64.1%), 73.0% is the SIMULATED population, and the gap is entirely SHA-256 testbench dedup (connected compiles collapse 3.08:1, disconnected 2.04:1). Wrong in one direction: the paper's stated mechanism -- that a disconnected partition makes COMPUTE bind non-sibling operands -- is false. build_schedule binds by node identity and DMEMAllocator's second pass gives every cross-PE child a dedicated receive slot above the local high-water mark, so binding is unconditional in alpha. I verified this statically on the emitted images of all 681 campaign configurations (1,010,895 COMPUTEs, zero violations) and on 300 random shattered assignments, which is stronger than the red team's 840 dynamic runs. The paper already contains the correct unconditional proof, at main.tex:1824-1833, where it uses it for C-sw and then forgets to use it for C-bind. Wrong in the other direction: the red team's conclusion that C-conn is not load-bearing is also wrong. Disconnection raises peak DMEM occupancy from a median of 10 slots (max 102) to a median of 25 (MAX 491) against a hard 512-entry DMEM that emit_sv_testbench does NOT resize (src/sprs_core.py:5384) while the fabric truncates DMEM addresses to 9 bits and SEND target addresses to 10 (btree_fsm_fast.sv:82, :629, :337). I constructed the counterexample the panel could not: FBT(512) on two PEs with leaves on PE0 and internals on PE1 needs 522 slots, and under the real 512-entry DMEM my ISA simulator returns a silently wrong root -- two DIFFERENT wrong roots for different delivery orders -- while the same image with a 4096-entry DMEM returns the canonical root every time. So a disconnected partition can change the root exactly when it drives peak DMEM past the ceiling, and the campaign's worst case was 491/512 with nothing in the pipeline checking it. Finally, the reviewers' remedy (re-run the campaign through compile()) is not available: repair_connectivity reassigns a median 51% of the tree, inflates peak per-PE node count by a median 1.86x and up to 304x, would push 82 of 437 disconnected configurations past the 512-instruction IMEM budget that all but one satisfy today, and actually INCREASES peak DMEM in 33 of them. The cheapest adequate fix is to describe the five stages that ran, replace C-conn with C-mem, delete Sec. 5.2's causal story and Remark and L8, and report the 491/512 margin. That is a net saving of about half a page.
